neighbours.label: the copula or verb slot right before an efficacy judgment (is [most effective], proven to [be ineffective], considered [acceptable])
fire: Doctors still disagree about which painkiller is most effective after knee surgery.
Several popular supplements have been found to be useless for preventing colds.
It remains unclear whether the new reading program is truly beneficial for young pupils.
In trials, the cheaper vaccine proved to be just as effective as the expensive one.
Experts asked which teaching method was most useful for students with dyslexia.
A longer course of antibiotics is not always considered necessary for mild infections.
The review asked whether acupuncture is helpful for chronic back pain at all.
Few of the proposed reforms appear likely to be effective in reducing crime.
quiet: Doctors still disagree about which hospital first performed knee surgery in the region.
Several popular supplements have been sold in pharmacies since the late nineties.
It remains unclear where the new reading program will be launched next year.
In trials, the cheaper vaccine was given to two thousand adults in three cities.
Experts asked which teaching method was first used in schools in the region.
A longer course of antibiotics usually lasts about ten days for mild infections.
The review asked how many clinics offer acupuncture for chronic back pain.
Few of the proposed reforms were discussed in the committee meeting on Tuesday.

notes: Top tokens is/be/most/considered before effective/acceptable/useful; the + pole's logit effect suppresses effective/beneficial/helpful, so the - pole promotes them. Probes 0.29-0.90 on efficacy frames; near misses with the same verb but a factual continuation scored 0.19-0.48, so near misses here avoid evaluation altogether.
